An interesting article, but as someone well versed in strategy games who doesn't like real time strategy games too much, those with a strong focus on the economy were easily those I liked the least. The problem I have with classical RTS games is that I have to go through all this fast clicking bullshit to get to the strategic decisions and more often than not I would lose MP games to the former, not the latter. That problem only gets worse when the whole economy thing gets involved. The MP RTS game I most enjoyed was Total War: Shogun 2 for a reason, and that reason is because I don't have to make more actions than what I can physically do. All Total War games work with zero economy in battle mode (because that would be completely retarded from a realism point of view), so you have to concentrate all your attention on your regiments. And these games aren't shallow either.

I don't think the problem is having economy micro-management alongside combat (see Civ games or Paradox grand strategy) the problem is having micro-management in real time. When I watch people playing these kinds of games it looks like they're playing a really contrived action game, not a strategy game. In fact it looks like they are fighting the interface and the lack of clever automation more than their opponent.
